slides.title: AI Coaching for Accelerating Human Skill Development with Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: RL-BASED AI COACHING FOR MOTOR-SKILL DEVELOPMENT
slides.highlight: This research explores an AI coaching framework using adaptive shared control and reinforcement learning to accelerate human motor-skill development, aligning with MOSAIC's goal of adaptive AI coaching to improve human proficiency.

card.one_liner: An RL-based AI coach accelerates human motor-skill development by strategically balancing assistance and productive failure.
card.key_idea: Formalizes coaching as a non-cooperative dynamic game using a probabilistic automaton to model skill evolution and a blending rule for adaptive shared control.
card.evaluation: User study (N=33) in FPV drone racing; L2C significantly reduced lap times (27.9%) and failures compared to RBF and MIA baselines.
card.limitation: Simulated learners may not capture the full variability of real human learning in more complex motor-skill settings.

slides.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models
slides.highlight: This work evaluates how small language models can assist in screening literature for social-physical human-robot interaction, supporting the RwB goal of advancing embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Small language models can augment systematic reviews by recovering relevant papers missed by human screeners.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using a unanimity ensemble of four locally deployed SLMs (≤1.5B parameters) as a conservative second-pass filter for title and abstract screening.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 32,000 spHRI records; the SLM ensemble identified 39 additional relevant papers (10.29% of final set) missed by humans.
card.limitation: SLMs cannot replace expert judgment due to a precision-recall tradeoff and lack of confidence scoring in binary outputs.

slides.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure
slides.highlight: This research explores inverted evaluation where LLM-powered robots rate their own interactions, providing insights into the boundary conditions of using AI to assess human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered robots can accurately rate user engagement but systematically fail to detect user strangeness/discomfort.
card.key_idea: An 'inverted evaluation' framework where LLMs complete standardized HRI questionnaires (HRI-CUES, Godspeed, RoSAS) from the robot's perspective using interaction transcripts and multimodal context.
card.evaluation: Tested via HRI-CUES dataset (1,522 evaluations across 5 LLMs) and a live Nao robot pilot (N=4) using Pearson r and ICC.
card.limitation: LLMs lack access to internal affective states, conflating philosophical engagement with comfort and failing on unexpressed strangeness.

slides.title: SupplyNet: Supporting Visual Exploratory Learning in Supply Chain via Contextual Multi-Agent Simulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework for simulating interdependent supply chain dynamics, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SupplyNet is a gamified visual simulation system for learning supply chain dynamics via LLM-driven multi-agent simulation.
card.key_idea: A contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework paired with a branching timeline for "what-if" exploration, an interactive network view, and a task-oriented analysis console.
card.evaluation: A user study comparing SupplyNet to a classic baseline simulation; results showed increased engagement and improved perceived understanding of supply chain dynamics.

slides.title: Real-Time Voice AI Hears but Does Not Listen
slides.tldr: EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE GAP IN VOICE AI
slides.highlight: This research identifies a disconnect between perception and action in real-time voice AI, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Real-time voice AIs prioritize spoken words over vocal delivery, ignoring critical emotional cues during decision-making.
card.key_idea: The 'emotional intelligence gap' where systems perceive emotions (distress, sarcasm) in single-turn diagnostics but disregard them in multi-turn consequential scenarios.
card.evaluation: Tested four production systems (GPT Realtime 2, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Qwen3.5 Omni Plus/Flash) using synthesized audio and human validation.
card.limitation: Prompting to attend to delivery only partially and inconsistently improved performance, failing to close the perception-action gap.

slides.title: Triadic Werewolf: A Jester Role for Multi-Hop Theory of Mind in LLMs
slides.highlight: This work introduces a triadic incentive structure in a social-deduction game to evaluate multi-hop theory of mind and multi-agent reasoning in LLMs, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: A new triadic Werewolf benchmark reveals LLMs struggle with multi-hop Theory of Mind reasoning.
card.key_idea: Introduces a Jester role with inverted utility (wins by being voted out), forcing models to reason across three competing faction goals instead of simple dyadic suspicion.
card.evaluation: 60 games using GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama-3.3-70B. Measured win rates, voting patterns, and a Jester self-learning loop. Results show high Jester win rates.
card.limitation: Small sample size (10 games per cell) leads to wide confidence intervals; evaluation limited to English language.

slides.title: Onconetix Announces Realbotix Optio and M-Series Humanoid Robot Pilot at Salamanca City Central School District
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT PILOT IN SCHOOL DISTRICT
slides.highlight: The pilot of Realbotix Optio and M-Series humanoid robots in a school district provides insights into embodied social robots for RwB.

slides.title: A Dynamic Coupling Theory of Expertise Through Thinking Flow and Workflow Evolution
slides.highlight: This paper proposes Workflow Cognition as a dynamic coupling of thinking flow and workflow evolution, providing a theoretical basis for estimating procedural and tacit skills within the MOSAIC project.

card.one_liner: Proposes Workflow Cognition, a theory where expertise emerges from the recursive coupling of thinking and action.
card.key_idea: Expertise is an emergent manifestation of 'Workflow Cognition,' defined as the dynamic, recursive interaction between 'Thinking Flow' (cognitive processes) and 'Workflow Evolution' (practical adaptation).
card.evaluation: Evaluated via comparative theoretical analyses across craft, creative, educational, and leadership domains; no empirical datasets or quantitative metrics are provided.
card.limitation: The paper is primarily theoretical and lacks empirical validation or quantitative testing of the proposed cognitive architecture.

slides.title: voxmap-studio: An open-source speaker diarization annotation tool with built-in cost instrumentation
slides.highlight: This tool provides a framework for labeling speaker diarization data with built-in cost instrumentation, supporting the development of the diarization and listener modeling components of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: An open-source speaker diarization tool that quantifies annotation effort via built-in cost instrumentation.
card.key_idea: A React-based tool featuring automatic initialization, uncertainty highlighting, and cost tracking (edit operations and time), with confirmation-gated exports and "phantom" attention checks to ensure data quality.
card.evaluation: Preliminary study on nine AMI audio files using one annotator; compared manual vs. assisted labeling via editOps, time, and DER.
card.limitation: Small sample size (single annotator, three files per condition), preventing broad statistical conclusions.

slides.title: A probabilistic framework for online test-time adaptation
slides.tldr: PROBABILISTIC FRAMEWORK FOR ONLINE TEST-TIME ADAPTATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a state-space modeling framework for online test-time adaptation to handle distributional shifts, supporting the ADAM-CHAT goal of creating agents that adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: A probabilistic state-space framework for online test-time adaptation of classifiers under distributional shift.
card.key_idea: Uses a state-space model combining source posteriors, Gibbs posteriors for unlabeled data observation, and dynamic linear model transitions to quantify uncertainty during sequential adaptation.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated. The text describes the theoretical framework and inference methods but does not provide experimental results or datasets.
card.limitation: Linear-Gaussian approximations may produce overconfident updates in highly non-convex parameter spaces due to single-point Taylor expansion.

slides.title: Advancing Speaker-Based Vocal Effort Classification with WavLM and Data Augmentation in Naturalistic Non-Calibrated Speech Recordings
slides.highlight: This work improves the classification of vocal effort levels (e.g., whisper, shout) using WavLM and soft labels. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: WavLM with data augmentation and Gaussian-neighbor soft labels achieves state-of-the-art vocal effort classification on AVID.
card.key_idea: Fine-tuned WavLM-Base using gradual unfreezing, waveform-level augmentations (e.g., MixUp, RIR), and Gaussian-neighbor soft labels to model the continuous nature of vocal effort and reduce boundary errors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AVID corpus using 10-fold group cross-validation. The best system achieved 78.22% mean accuracy, outperforming wav2vec2 and HuBERT.
card.limitation: The study is limited to the AVID corpus, and over-aggressive mixing (e.g., MixUp alpha=0.8) can blur category boundaries.

slides.title: GROVE: Grounded Pedestrian Simulation via Natural Language for Interactive Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: GROVE enables the generation of realistic, socially challenging pedestrian scenarios via natural language, aiding the training of social robot navigation to narrow the sim2real gap. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: GROVE is a text-to-scenario framework for high-fidelity pedestrian simulation to train social robot navigation.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs, RAG-based behavior tree generation, and Theta* global planning to translate natural language prompts into realistic, socially complex pedestrian behaviors across three temporal horizons.
card.evaluation: Qualitative trajectory analysis and VLM-based scoring (GPT-5) against Text-Crowd and TRACE in hospital, office, and residential environments; GROVE showed superior prompt alignment.
card.limitation: High computational inference costs and a reliance on static obstacle maps, ignoring dynamic environmental changes like moving furniture.

slides.title: RECAST: Model Reconstruction via Counterfactual-Aware Wasserstein Geometry under Limited Data
slides.highlight: RECAST uses counterfactual-aware Wasserstein optimization to reconstruct black-box models for fairness auditing, supporting the societal-scale impact analysis goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: RECAST reconstructs black-box models using Wasserstein barycentric prototypes to handle limited data and one-sided counterfactuals.
card.key_idea: It treats counterfactuals as soft cross-class constraints, optimizing 2-Wasserstein barycenters as class prototypes to create a behavior-centric surrogate stable under distributional uncertainty.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four real-world datasets (Adult, COMPAS, HELOC, California Housing) against baselines like SAMPLES and CCA using fidelity and robustness metrics.
card.limitation: The target decision boundary is statistically non-identifiable under one-sided CF access, meaning it recovers behavioral equivalence rather than a unique ground-truth boundary.

slides.title: Virtual Simulation for Mental Health
slides.tldr: VIRTUAL SIMULATION FOR SAFE MENTAL HEALTH INTERVENTIONS
slides.highlight: This work explores virtual simulation and agent-based modeling to safely test mental health interventions and evaluate community-level outcomes, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Virtual simulation enables safe, controlled experimentation and training for mental health interventions to prevent real-world harm.
card.key_idea: Uses agent-based modeling for community-level outcomes and embodied, controlled virtual spaces for individual training, guided by a grounded human-centered design approach.

slides.title: Do more heads imply better performance? An empirical study of team thought leaders' impact on scientific team performance
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF THOUGHT LEADERSHIP ON TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This study examines how the number of thought leaders affects team impact and disruptiveness, providing insights into group dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on team state and engagement.

card.one_liner: More thought leaders in scientific teams have an inverted U-shaped impact on performance and reduce disruptiveness.
card.key_idea: Analyzes 140,000+ PLOS papers, defining thought leaders via contribution statements to examine their effect on team impact and disruptiveness using correlational and causal perspectives.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using over 140,000 papers from PLOS journals, measuring team impact and disruptiveness across various team compositions.

slides.title: When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY PROMPTING IMPACTS MULTI-AGENT LLM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This study examines how personality traits in LLM agents influence communication styles and task outcomes, providing insights into the social dynamics and engagement of hybrid human-AI team states for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Personality prompting affects LLM team outcomes based on task structure, with structured outputs buffering against degradation.
card.key_idea: Low-agreeableness prompting shifts communication toward exploration/disagreement. This degrades performance in unstructured tasks (research, bargaining) but has minimal impact on structured tasks (coding) due to artifact-mediated buffering.
card.evaluation: Tested Claude, GPT-4o, Grok-3, and DeepSeek on MultiAgentBench (coding, research, bargaining) using milestone counts and agreement rates; results show significant domain-specific variance.
card.limitation: Standard personality prompts use negatively loaded adjectives that may trigger safety-adjacent responses, inflating adversarial behavior beyond genuine trait effects.

slides.title: When Multi-Robot Systems Meet Agentic AI: Towards Embodied Collective Intelligence
slides.tldr: EMBODIED COLLECTIVE INTELLIGENCE FOR MULTI-ROBOT SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: This work proposes Embodied Collective Intelligence (ECI) to enable robot teams to share world context and skill experience, supporting the RwB goal of advancing embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes Embodied Collective Intelligence (ECI) to share agentic states across multi-robot teams for enhanced collaboration.
card.key_idea: ECI organizes shared team resources through Co-Perception (world memory), Co-Action (task-state ledgers), and Co-Evolution (shared skill libraries) to enable state inheritance for new robots.
card.evaluation: A target-object navigation study using Habitat-Matterport 3D showed that robots inheriting merged team memory achieved higher success rates (77.1%-82.5%) than those without.
card.limitation: The case study only evaluated world-memory inheritance; Co-Action and Co-Evolution remain conceptual and not yet fully measured.

slides.title: Long-Term Prediction of Local and Global Human Motion with Occlusion Recovery
slides.highlight: This research proposes a transformer-based model for local and global human motion prediction and occlusion recovery, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A non-autoregressive transformer for long-term local and global human motion prediction with occlusion recovery capabilities.
card.key_idea: Uses spatio-temporal attention and joint-separate positional encoding to predict future poses non-autoregressively, employing learnable tokens to recover missing joints caused by occlusions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Human3.6M, AMASS, and HA4M using MPJPE and MAE; outperformed standard Transformer and other non-autoregressive baselines in long-term prediction.
card.limitation: Struggles with unpredictable motion transitions between different actions and complex, high-variability arm movements due to data scarcity.

slides.title: Designing Trustworthy LLM-based Wellbeing Recommendation through Controllable Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a system-level framework for controllable LLM interactions to improve intent alignment and trust calibration, supporting the MOSAIC goal of aligning human-AI intent.

card.one_liner: A framework for trustworthy wellbeing recommendations using explicit interaction constraints instead of implicit LLM adaptation.
card.key_idea: A modular architecture that separates LLM generation from an interaction layer governing guidance strategy, directness, explanation style, and responsibility framing to ensure controllability and transparency.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated. The paper proposes an evaluation perspective focusing on self-efficacy, perceived agency, and trust rather than reporting specific results.
card.limitation: Challenges remain in specifying dynamic constraints and integrating user control without increasing user burden or undermining system support.
